content.summary: Implementation plan for: investigate provider timeout sleep/wake behavior via config A/B isolation and error mapping gap tests

data.goal: Prove (or disprove) that the default no-timeout config path causes indefinite hangs after sleep/wake, and map exact gaps in error classification that prevent proper retry/UX feedback.
data.learning_milestone: After WI-03 completes, we will know: (1) whether the default path truly hangs forever, (2) exactly which error types escape proper classification, (3) whether TimeoutError from AbortSignal.timeout gets retried or surfaces as UnknownError. This tells us whether a default timeout + expanded error handling is the right fix.
data.approach: The provider fetch wrapper in provider.ts:1044-1082 has three timeout paths: no config (no timeout), explicit number (AbortSignal.timeout), explicit false (no timeout). The default path — which all users without custom config hit — provides zero abort protection. After sleep/wake, TCP connections die silently; without AbortSignal.timeout, fetch hangs forever. The error mapping in message-v2.ts:722+ only handles AbortError and ECONNRESET specifically, but TimeoutError (from AbortSignal.timeout) and ETIMEDOUT/EPIPE (from kernel) are not handled. We test each path in isolation, simulate the hang, map the error classification gaps, then produce a fix proposal.

changes_required.change: New test file: proves 3 timeout config paths behave as analyzed
New test file: simulates hung fetch, proves hang with no timeout, proves recovery with timeout
New test file: maps exactly how TimeoutError, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE are classified through fromError + retryable
Fix proposal document with exact changes, risk assessment, and validation plan

technical.why_hard: The fetch wrapper is defined inline inside getSDK() closure — not directly exportable. Tests need to either use Instance.provide with a mock server or extract the logic.
technical.mitigation: Follow existing test pattern (tmpdir + Instance.provide + config JSON) from provider.test.ts. Alternatively, test the logic by constructing equivalent closures.

technical.why_hard: Bun's AbortSignal.timeout may behave differently from Node.js spec. The DOMException name/message may vary.
technical.mitigation: WI-02 will empirically verify what AbortSignal.timeout(N) actually throws in Bun when triggered.

technical.why_hard: Bun SystemError is not a standard JS Error — it has .code, .syscall, .errno fields. Constructing one in a test may not match real runtime shape.
technical.mitigation: Use Object.assign on Error to add .code/.syscall properties, matching what fromError checks.

dependencies: No external API keys needed — all tests use mocked fetch
risk_factors: If Bun's AbortSignal.timeout doesn't throw standard DOMException, error classification tests may need adjustment

open_questions: Does Bun's fetch with timeout:false genuinely disable ALL timeouts, or does it only disable Bun's default (which may already be infinity)?
When AbortSignal.timeout fires during an SSE stream (not initial fetch), does the SSE retry logic in serverSentEvents.gen.ts catch it before processor.ts?
Is there a Bun-specific fetch timeout that applies even when timeout:false is set? (ref: github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/16682)

unit: WI-01: 3 test cases for timeout config paths
WI-02: 3 test cases for sleep simulation + error production
WI-03: 5+ test cases for error classification mapping
integration: After fix: manual sleep/wake test with real provider to verify retry behavior

risks.risk: Tests may not perfectly simulate real sleep/wake TCP death
risks.mitigation: Use never-resolving promises as proxy; document this limitation in test comments

risks.risk: Fix proposal may conflict with providers that legitimately need infinite timeout (e.g. very long generation)
risks.mitigation: Proposal will recommend timeout:false as explicit opt-out, not remove the option

risks.risk: SSE retry layer may interact with session retry layer causing double-retry
risks.mitigation: WI-04 will analyze this interaction explicitly
